memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So the Lord God said to the serpent, "Because you have done this, cursed are you above all livestock and all wild animals! You will crawl on your belly and you will eat dust all the days of your life." — Gen 3:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice something important about the order here. When God turns to bring judgment, He begins with the serpent — and unlike with Adam and Eve, He asks no question. There is no "What have you done?" for the tempter. God simply pronounces the curse. The deceiver is not invited to explain, because there is no path of restoration being offered to him.

The picture of crawling on the belly and eating dust was a well-understood image in the ancient world of total defeat and humiliation. To "lick the dust" was the posture of a conquered enemy (Ps 72:9). God is declaring that the serpent, who exalted himself to challenge God's word, will be brought low. Evil may seem to win for a moment in the garden, but its end is defeat and shame.

We should be careful here not to over-read the verse. This is God's judgment on the tempter, not a lesson about literal snakes, and certainly not license for us to fear or despise any creature. The heart of it is this: God takes evil seriously, and He will deal with it.

Dear friend, take comfort. The God who judged the serpent in the garden has not lost His grip on evil today. Every power that opposes Him is already on the path to defeat, and one day, in Christ, the enemy will be crushed completely under our feet (Rom 16:20). Evil does not have the last word. God does.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does it comfort you to know that God takes evil seriously and will judge it?
2. Where do you need to trust that God is still in control, even when evil seems to prosper?
3. How does the promise of the enemy's final defeat give you hope today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are a just God who does not ignore evil but will deal with it fully. When wickedness seems to win, help me to trust that its end is already decided. Thank You that in Christ the enemy will be crushed completely. Amen.
